Shift by shift
Overtime, on-call and extra pay (optional)

Did you work overtime, get called back in, or do on-call? Add it here and it’s included in your estimate. Most people can skip this.

Rates used (only change these if your payslip is different)

These start from the Nurses (SA Public Sector) Award and the 2022 enterprise agreement, so most people never need to touch them.

Where these come from: overtime 150% for the first three hours and 200% after, Monday to Saturday, and 200% on Sunday (Award clause 5.4.3); public holiday work 250% (clause 6.3.7); recall has a three-hour minimum (agreement clause 7.1.2); on-call and in-charge amounts are the January 2025 figures in the 2022 agreement (clauses 9.5.2 and 9.4). A newer agreement may have changed them.

Rates, breaks and public holidays (edit)
About this estimate

Who it’s for: employees of the South Australian public health system (SA Health) who are paid under the Nursing/Midwifery (South Australian Public Sector) Enterprise Agreement 2022. It isn’t suitable for private, aged care, agency or interstate employers. The rates are the permanent rates; casual rates are different.

What it’s based on: the ANMF SA Branch pay rates for that agreement (Permanent rates, “4% Interim Administrative Increase effective first full pay period on or after 1 January 2026”). The “1 October 2026” pay table adds the further 2% interim increase to those rates; I calculated it rather than reading it from a published table, so check it against your payslip. Penalty percentages are those in the same table: afternoon 112.5%, night 120.5%, Saturday 150%, Sunday 175%, public holiday 250%. Night loading, shift lengths and breaks follow the agreement as I’ve read it, and may not match every roster.

Other BOSS shift codes: codes other than E, L, N and N2 use the times and unpaid break from the BOSS code list. I give them late loading if they finish after 6pm, and night loading if they finish after midnight. That is my reading, not the agreement, so check those shifts against your payslip.

Limits: gross pay is base pay, penalties and the professional development allowance for worked shifts. You enter your own salary sacrifice and other deductions. The professional development allowance follows clause 5.2 of the agreement ($2,547.70 a year from 1 July 2025, rising with the salary increases and paid pro rata by hours). It doesn’t apply to casuals, AINs or graduates in a transition program, so set it to 0 if that’s you. It excludes annual leave, other allowances, overtime and recalls. Tax uses the ATO’s annualised withholding method with the tax-free threshold and Medicare levy, and ignores any study loan, so it can differ from your payslip by a few dollars. Pay periods are counted in fortnights from the first day of the roster.

Not advice: this is a planning aid, not financial, tax or legal advice, and it is not affiliated with or endorsed by SA Health, the ANMF or any salary packaging provider. The agreement may change when it is replaced. Your payslip and the agreement are always the authority.

Family calendar

More settings

When you try a swap, the app checks your calendar and warns about anything close to the new shift. This is the gap it leaves for getting to work and home again. With 30 minutes, an appointment that starts 20 minutes after your shift ends is flagged, because you couldn’t get there in time. Set it to 0 to only flag events that overlap the shift itself.

Google Calendar

Connect once to add your shifts straight to your calendar and check swaps against your family calendar. Your roster stays in this browser. Google will ask to view and edit events on your calendars, and the app only adds, updates or removes shifts it created itself.

One-time setup
  1. In Google Cloud Console, create a project and turn on the Google Calendar API.
  2. Set up the OAuth consent screen as External and add your own Google account as a test user. In test mode, sign-in expires about every 7 days.
  3. Create Credentials → OAuth client ID → Web application. Under Authorised JavaScript origins add:
  4. Paste the Client ID below.

Google sign-in doesn’t work from a file on your computer. Open this page from a web address (for example free hosting such as GitHub Pages), or on your computer from http://localhost:8000 by running python -m http.server 8000 in the folder that holds this file.

Not connected.

On iPhone, Google sign-in can fail when the app is opened from the home screen. If it does, open the page in Safari to connect and add your shifts.

Outlook and Microsoft 365

Connect once, then add your shifts to your Outlook calendar with one tap. Your roster stays on this device, and the app only adds, updates or removes its own shifts.

Not connected.

Some work and school accounts block outside apps. If sign-in is blocked, use the calendar file below or ask your IT team.

Apple Calendar and others

Apple doesn’t let web apps write to Calendar directly, so this is a two-tap add: download the file, then tap it. It also works with most other calendar apps. Nothing is uploaded anywhere.

How to add it
  1. iPhone or iPad: tap the downloaded file, then Add All.
  2. Mac: open the file and choose which calendar to add it to.
  3. Other apps: open the file, or import it from the app’s calendar settings.

Tip: add your shifts to their own new calendar called Roster Hero. If your roster changes, delete that calendar and import the new file, so you don’t end up with doubles.

Help

Report a problem, install the app, back up your data and read the policies.

Report a problem

Something wrong or not working? This opens an email to the person who runs the app, with the details already filled in. You can read and change it before sending.

Tick this if the problem is about your roster or pay. Leave it off to share only technical details.

Install on your phone

Add it to your home screen so it opens like an app.

  • iPhone (Safari): tap the Share button, then Add to Home Screen.
  • Android (Chrome): tap the menu (three dots), then Install app or Add to Home screen.

You’re on an iPhone: use Safari for this, not another browser.

Back up and restore

Your roster and settings live only on this device. A backup file lets you move them to a new phone or recover them if your browser data is cleared. The file stays with you and is never sent to us.

      Terms of use

      Last updated 21 November 2026

      Draft for review. Have a lawyer check this before launch, and fill in the business details in APP_CONFIG.

      Who we are

      (ABN ) runs . In these terms, “we” and “us” mean that business, and “you” means the person using the app. You can contact us at .

      What the app does

      reads a roster from a picture you choose, shows you the shifts it found so you can check them, and can add those shifts to your calendar and estimate your pay.

      Estimates only, not advice

      Pay and take-home figures are estimates to help you plan. They are not payroll, tax, financial or legal advice, and they may be wrong or out of date, including when an enterprise agreement or tax rates change. Your payslip and your agreement always come first. We are not connected to, and are not endorsed by, SA Health, the ANMF or any employer or union.

      Check your shifts

      Reading a picture can make mistakes. You are responsible for checking every week against your real roster before you save it or add it to a calendar, and for turning up to the shifts your employer rosters you on.

      Subscriptions and payments

      Some features need a paid plan. Plans renew automatically at the end of each billing period (monthly, 6 months or 12 months) until you cancel. A free trial, if offered, converts to a paid plan unless you cancel before it ends. You can cancel at any time from Manage subscription, and you keep access until the end of the period you’ve paid for. Payments are taken by Stripe, and we never see or store your card details. Prices are in Australian dollars. Nothing in these terms limits your rights under the Australian Consumer Law, including any right to a refund or remedy for a fault.

      Refer a friend

      If you invite a friend and they become a paying subscriber, you may earn free months, up to the limit shown in the app. Credit has no cash value and can’t be transferred. Please only send invitations to people you know, one at a time, and don’t spam or mislead anyone. We may change or end the referral offer, and we may withhold credit we reasonably believe was earned unfairly.

      Using the app fairly

      Don’t misuse the app, try to get around the subscription, copy or resell it, or use it to break the law or anyone’s rights.

      Other services

      If you connect Google Calendar or Outlook, those services have their own terms. We don’t control them and aren’t responsible for how they work.

      Availability and changes

      We work to keep the app running, but we can’t promise it will always be available or error free. We may change the app, the plans or these terms. If a change is significant we’ll tell you in the app, and by continuing to use the app you accept the updated terms.

      Our responsibility

      To the extent the law allows, we aren’t liable for loss caused by relying on an estimate, a misread shift or a calendar problem, or for indirect or consequential loss. Nothing here excludes liability that can’t be excluded by law.

      Law

      These terms are governed by the laws of South Australia.

      Privacy policy

      Last updated 21 November 2026

      Draft for review. Have a lawyer check this before launch, and fill in the business details in APP_CONFIG.

      The short version

      Your roster picture is read on your phone and is never uploaded. Your shifts, pay settings and deductions are saved on your phone only. We only hold the details needed to run your subscription.

      What stays on your phone

      Your roster picture, the shifts read from it, your pay point, salary sacrifice and deduction amounts, your swap history and your settings. We can’t see them. If you clear your data or remove the app, they’re gone.

      What we collect

      When you subscribe, Stripe collects your email address and payment details so it can take payment and send receipts. We keep your email address, your plan and its end date through Stripe, and a referral code made from your Stripe customer record. If you contact support, we keep your message and reply. We don’t use ads or analytics trackers, and we don’t sell your information.

      Who else sees what

      • Stripe processes payments and holds your email, plan and billing history.
      • Cloudflare runs the small service that confirms your subscription, so it handles your requests when you subscribe, restore or manage your plan.
      • Email delivery: if you ask for a restore link, your email address passes through our email delivery provider.
      • Google or Microsoft: only if you connect a calendar. The shifts you choose to add are sent to that calendar, and the connection is used only for that.
      • Reading engine files: the picture-reading tool is downloaded from a public content network when you first scan. Your picture is not sent anywhere.

      Keeping it safe

      Payments run through Stripe’s secure checkout, and we never see your card. Anything we hold is kept with the providers above. If we find out about a breach that is likely to cause you serious harm, we’ll tell you and the regulator as the law requires.

      Your choices

      You can see, correct or ask us to delete the information we hold about you by emailing . To erase what’s on your phone, use “Delete all my data from this device” in Help. We aim to follow the Australian Privacy Principles.

      Changes

      If we change this policy we’ll update the date above and tell you in the app if the change matters.
